summary: Munich-based neobroker Scalable Capital raised €60 million ($65 million) in a Balderton-led round at a flat $1.4 billion valuation, matching its 2021 valuation despite becoming four or five times bigger. The money will fund expansion in its six active European countries and into new ones, as competition grows from Trade Republic, Robinhood, Freetrade and Lightyear. Co-CEO Erik Podzuweit says the company is not pursuing a banking license and is focusing on products and new markets.
one_line: Scalable Capital raised €60M ($65M) led by Balderton at a flat $1.4B valuation, to expand across Europe amid rising neobroker competition.
key_facts: Scalable Capital, a Munich startup, raised €60 million in equity, equal to $65 million at the article's rates.
Balderton led the round, with participation from HV Capital out of its new growth fund and other unnamed existing backers.
The valuation is flat at $1.4 billion, the same as its 2021 round of $180 million led by Tencent, with BlackRock, HV and Tengelmann participating.
Co-CEO Erik Podzuweit says Scalable Capital is 'four or five times bigger' than it was two years ago.
Scalable Capital is active in Germany, Austria, Italy, France, Spain and Netherlands and plans to expand into more countries.
The company has 1.2 million savings plans, over 600,000 customers and close to €17 billion under management.
Users can invest in 8,000 stocks, 2,500 ETFs and 3,500 funds; ETFs are the most popular product.
Scalable Capital has now raised more than $345 million in total.
Trade Republic, Scalable's biggest startup rival, secured a full banking license from the European Central Bank and was last valued at $5.3 billion in June 2022.
Scalable Capital is not pursuing a banking license; Podzuweit says it is leaner and faster working with partners such as ING.
Robinhood opened a U.K. office late last month and launched crypto trading in the EU; Freetrade and Lightyear are other U.K. players with European ambitions.
Scalable Capital's average user age is 35.
Balderton general partner Rana Yared is joining Scalable Capital's board with this round.
